title: Network Biology Analyses and Dynamic Modeling of Gene Regulatory Networks under Drought Stress Reveal Major Transcriptional Regulators in Arabidopsis.
authors: Kumar, Nilesh; Mishra, Bharat K; Liu, Jinbao; Mohan, Binoop; Thingujam, Doni; Pajerowska-Mukhtar, Karolina M; Mukhtar, M Shahid
one_liner_zh: 该文通过共表达网络和动态数学建模研究拟南芥干旱胁迫下的基因调控网络，识别转录因子及其靶基因，但未涉及蛋白质-DNA三维互作建模或AI/物理模拟方法，仅属网络层面的转录调控分析，与TF-DNA结合机制研究关联较弱。
abstract: Drought is one of the most serious abiotic stressors in the environment, restricting agricultural production by reducing plant growth, development, and productivity. To investigate such a complex and multifaceted stressor and its effects on plants, a systems biology-based approach is necessitated, entailing the generation of co-expression networks, identification of high-priority transcription factors (TFs), dynamic mathematical modeling, and computational simulations. Here, we studied a high-resolution drought transcriptome of Arabidopsis. We identified distinct temporal transcriptional signatures and demonstrated the involvement of specific biological pathways. Generation of a large-scale co-expression network followed by network centrality analyses identified 117 TFs that possess critical properties of hubs, bottlenecks, and high clustering coefficient nodes. Dynamic transcriptional regulatory modeling of integrated TF targets and transcriptome datasets uncovered major transcriptional events during the course of drought stress. Mathematical transcriptional simulations allowed us to ascertain the activation status of major TFs, as well as the transcriptional intensity and amplitude of their target genes. Finally, we validated our predictions by providing experimental evidence of gene expression under drought stress for a set of four TFs and their major target genes using qRT-PCR. Taken together, we provided a systems-level perspective on the dynamic transcriptional regulation during drought stress in Arabidopsis and uncovered numerous novel TFs that could potentially be used in future genetic crop engineering programs.
abstract_zh: 干旱是环境中最严重的非生物胁迫因子之一，通过减少植物生长、发育和生产力来限制农业生产。为了研究这种复杂且多方面的胁迫及其对植物的影响，需要采用基于系统生物学的方法，包括生成共表达网络、识别高优先级转录因子（TFs）、动态数学建模和计算模拟。在此，我们研究了拟南芥的高分辨率干旱转录组。我们识别了不同的时间转录特征，并证明了特定生物途径的参与。通过生成大规模共表达网络并进行网络中心性分析，我们鉴定了117个具有枢纽、瓶颈和高聚类系数节点关键特性的转录因子。对整合的转录因子靶标和转录组数据集进行动态转录调控建模，揭示了干旱胁迫过程中的主要转录事件。数学转录模拟使我们能够确定主要转录因子的激活状态，以及其靶基因的转录强度和幅度。最后，我们通过qRT-PCR对四个转录因子及其主要靶基因在干旱胁迫下的基因表达提供了实验证据，验证了我们的预测。综合来看，我们提供了拟南芥干旱胁迫期间动态转录调控的系统级视角，并发现了许多可能在未来遗传作物工程计划中应用的新型转录因子。
